ggml.thread_check: in the last 1 s before exit (inside the timed loop): threads_timed (most threads seen) must be 1, and threads other than the main one at most 5% of its CPU time (process minus main thread, /proc ticks, cpu_ticks.timed_window); threads_max and the whole-run ticks include test-backend-ops' test-data init threads, which run before timing
ggml.statistic: test-backend-ops perf: mean time per run over >= 1 s of back-to-back runs of the op on the same tensors; time_s = median of runs_per_case such means; not interleaved with the other implementations

protocol.interleaved: implementations of a case alternate call by call
protocol.clock: core GHz sampled on the same thread (5 ms dependent add-reg-reg chain, 1 cycle/add) before, every 5 rounds and after each case; per-cycle rates use the median
protocol.stream: float32 arrays of max(4x LLC, 64 MiB) each, same warm-up/reps/clock protocol as the kernels, single thread on the pinned core: read = sum of one array, 4 bytes per element, read by every read-only loop we have (interleaved): 2, 4, 8 and 16 parts side by side, and with the AVX2 kernels the GEMV row pattern (rows of 4096 floats, 4 or 8 rows side by side, 32-byte loads; 8 rows with the next group prefetched); stream_read_gbs is the fastest (the roof for read-only kernels such as GEMV: a lower bound on the core's read limit); triad a = b + s*c, 12 bytes per element (STREAM convention, no write-allocate; stream_triad_gbs). *_allcore_gbs: OpenMP builds with more than one usable CPU only (part sums), else null
protocol.gemv: y = x·Wᵀ, one row x, W [N, K]; gb_per_s = (weights + x + y bytes) / median time (Q8_0: 34 bytes per 32 weights); per-case roof: the read-stream loops (protocol.stream) timed interleaved with the case's implementations, roof_read_gbs = the fastest; pct_stream_read = gb_per_s / roof_read_gbs; pct_stream_triad = gb_per_s / machine.stream_triad_gbs (once per run); roof_unstable: an implementation above 105% of its case's roof; weights rotate: ceil(2 x LLC / weight bytes) copies (weight_copies, at least 1), the next copy on every call of any implementation, so no call finds its weights in the last-level cache (ggml's test-backend-ops reuses its weights)
